experimental_question: Can a local model identify a latent retry-policy regression when a later dependency slowdown triggers delayed queue amplification, while rejecting a loud unrelated error?

construct_validity.intended_construct: Source-grounded diagnosis of delayed, nonlinear failure propagation across a worker and queue system.
observable_proxies: separation of retry-policy root cause from dependency-slowdown trigger
ordered reconstruction from immediate retries through queue amplification to user impact
use of exact cross-file event citations
rejection of broker-outage and test-tenant TLS explanations
recognition that full recovery follows both rollback and queue drain
bounded impact, uncertainty and mechanism-specific remediation
construct_validity.validation_evidence: The independent reference passes every essential check; targeted mutations of cause, trigger, amplification evidence, distractor rejection, recovery state and unsupported claims fail deterministically.
known_blind_spots: deterministic verification does not score prose quality
one retry pattern cannot establish general incident-response competence

criterion_groups.description: The report follows the strict v2 contract.
Impact onset, observation boundary and full recovery are evidenced in UTC.
The latent retry regression, exposing slowdown, amplification and effects remain distinct.
Citations exist in declared files and cover the full causal and recovery chain.
Broker and notification explanations are rejected using supplied counter-evidence.
Observed delay is reported without invented loss or counts.
Actions reduce retry amplification and improve detection under dependency degradation.

reporting_limits: Offline fixture qualification is not model evidence.
One excluded smoke per system is required before a measured multi-case sweep.
Do not infer reliability or latency tails from a Capability Sweep.
Compare harnesses only as complete deployed systems.
